<output>
# dua (Disk Usage Analyzer)

**dua** is a tool to conveniently learn about the usage of disk space of a given directory. It's parallel by default and will max out your SSD, providing relevant information as fast as possible. Optionally delete superfluous data, and do so more quickly than `rm`.

[![asciicast](https://asciinema.org/a/kDnXUOeqBxZVMoWuFNqzfpeey.svg)](https://asciinema.org/a/kDnXUOeqBxZVMoWuFNqzfpeey)

## Installation

### Binary Release 

#### MacOS

```sh
curl -LSfs https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Byron/dua-cli/master/ci/install.sh | \
    sh -s -- --git Byron/dua-cli --crate dua --tag v2.29.0
```

#### MacOS via [MacPorts](https://www.macports.org):
```sh
sudo port selfupdate
sudo port install dua-cli
```

#### MacOS via [Homebrew](https://brew.sh)
```sh
brew update
brew install dua-cli
```

#### Linux

Linux requires the target to be specified explicitly to obtain the MUSL build.

```sh
curl -LSfs https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Byron/dua-cli/master/ci/install.sh | \
    sh -s -- --git Byron/dua-cli --target x86_64-unknown-linux-musl --crate dua --tag v2.29.0
```

#### Windows via [Scoop](https://scoop.sh/)
```sh
scoop install dua
```

#### Windows via [WinGet](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/package-manager/winget/)
```sh
winget install Byron.dua-cli
```

#### Pre-built Binaries

See the [releases section](https://github.com/Byron/dua-cli/releases) for manual installation of a binary, pre-built for many platforms.

#### VoidLinux
Via `xbps` on your VoidLinux system.

```
xbps-install dua-cli
```

#### Fedora
Via `dnf` on your Fedora system.

```
sudo dnf install dua-cli
```

#### Arch Linux
Via `pacman` on your ArchLinux system.

```
sudo pacman -S dua-cli
```

#### NixOS
https://search.nixos.org/packages?channel=23.11&show=dua&from=0&size=50&sort=relevance&type=packages&query=dua

Nix-shell (temporary)

```
nix-shell -p dua
```

NixOS configuration

```
  environment.systemPackages = [
    pkgs.dua
  ];
```

#### NetBSD
Via `pkgin` on your NetBSD system.

```
pkgin install dua-cli
```

Or, building from source

```
cd /usr/pkgsrc/sysutils/dua-cli
make install
```

#### Windows

You will find pre-built binaries for Windows in the [releases section](https://github.com/Byron/dua-cli/releases).

#### x-cmd

[x-cmd](https://www.x-cmd.com/) is a **toolbox for Posix Shell**, offering a lightweight package manager built using shell and awk.
```sh
x env use dua
```
- Additionally, the [`x dua ...`](https://www.x-cmd.com/pkg/dua#dua) command is available, which automatically installs `dua` without affecting the environment, such as not modifying the `PATH` variable.

## Usage

```bash
# count the space used in the current working directory
dua
# count the space used in all directories that are not hidden
dua *
# learn about additional functionality
dua aggregate --help
```

### Interactive Mode

Launch into interactive mode with the `i` or `interactive` subcommand. Get help on keyboard
shortcuts with `?`.
Use this mode to explore, and/or to delete files and directories to release disk space.

Please note that great care has been taken to prevent accidental deletions due to a multi-stage
process, which makes this mode viable for exploration.

```bash
dua i
dua interactive
```

## Limitations

* Does not show symbolic links at all if no path is provided when invoking `dua`
  * in an effort to skip symbolic links, for now there are pruned and are not used as a root. Symbolic links will be shown if they
    are not a traversal root, but will not be followed.
* Interactive mode only looks good in dark terminals (see [this issue](https://github.com/Byron/dua-cli/issues/13))
* File names in main window are not truncated if too large. They are cut off on the right.
* There are plenty of examples in test fixtures which don't render correctly in interactive mode.
  This can be due to graphemes not interpreted correctly. With Chinese characters for instance,
  column sizes are not correctly computed, leading to certain columns not being shown.
  In other cases, the terminal gets things wrong - I use alacritty, and with certain characters it
  performs worse than, say iTerm3.
* In interactive mode, you will need about 60MB of memory for 1 million entries in the graph.
* In interactive mode, the maximum amount of files is limited to 2^32 - 1 entries.

## Similar Programs 

* **CLI:**
  * `du`
  * [`dust`](https://github.com/bootandy/dust)
  * [`dutree`](https://github.com/nachoparker/dutree)
  * [`pdu`](https://github.com/KSXGitHub/parallel-disk-usage)
* **TUI:**
  * [`ncdu`](https://dev.yorhel.nl/ncdu)
  * [`gdu`](https://github.com/dundee/gdu)

def run(*args, cwd="/workspace"):
    r = subprocess.run([EXE]+list(args), capture_output=True, text=True, cwd=cwd)
    return r
import os
# Observe:
# binary for 1024 -> "1024   B" not KiB, but 1025 -> "1.00 KiB", 1048576 -> "1024.00 KiB" (not MiB!)
# So binary thresholds are weird: stays in B until >1024? And stays in KiB even at 1MiB?
# Check larger: 1MiB+1, 1GiB?
os.system("python3 -c \"open('/tmp/fmt2/f2m','wb').write(b'x'*(2*1024*1024)); open('/tmp/fmt2/f10m','wb').write(b'x'*(10*1024*1024))\" && ls -lh /tmp/fmt2/")
for f in ["/tmp/fmt2/f2m","/tmp/fmt2/f10m"]:
    for fmt in ["binary","metric","bytes","gb","gib","mb","mib"]:
        r=run("-f",fmt,"-A",f)
        print(f"{f} {fmt}: {repr(r.stdout)}")
    print("---")
# Also check binary for 1048576*1024 = 1GiB boundary?
# Let's just test apparent sizes via truncate to avoid writing huge files
os.system("truncate -s 1073741824 /tmp/fmt2/f1g && truncate -s 1073741825 /tmp/fmt2/f1g1 && ls -lh /tmp/fmt2/f1g*")
for f in ["/tmp/fmt2/f1g","/tmp/fmt2/f1g1"]:
    for fmt in ["binary","metric","gb","gib","mb","mib"]:
        r=run("-f",fmt,"-A",f)
        print(f"{f} {fmt}: {repr(r.stdout)}")

import subprocess, os
EXE="/workspace/executable"
def run(*a, cwd="/workspace"):
    import subprocess
    r=subprocess.run([EXE]+list(a), capture_output=True, text=True, cwd=cwd)
    return r
def strip(s):
    return s.replace("\x1b[32m","").replace("\x1b[39m","").replace("\x1b[36m","")
def raw(s):
    return repr(s)

# Color for symlink dir as multiple inputs
os.system("ls -l /tmp/linktest/")
for args in [
    ("/tmp/linktest/linkdir","/tmp/linktest/real"),
    ("/tmp/linktest/linkfile","/tmp/linktest/real/f"),
    ("/tmp/linktest/linkdir",),
    ("-f","bytes","/tmp/linktest/linkdir","/tmp/linktest/real"),
]:
    r=run(*args)
    print(f"ARGS {args} -> {raw(r.stdout)} rc={r.returncode}")

# Stats for special files
os.system("rm -rf /tmp/special2 && mkdir -p /tmp/special2 && mkfifo /tmp/special2/fifo && touch /tmp/special2/empty && ls -l /tmp/special2/")
r=run("aggregate","--stats","/tmp/special2")
print("special stats:", raw(strip(r.stdout)), repr(r.stderr))
r=run("-f","bytes","aggregate","--stats","/tmp/special2")
print("special bytes stats:", raw(strip(r.stdout)), repr(r.stderr))

# Log file more
os.system("rm -f /tmp/log1 /tmp/log2")
r=run("-A","-f","bytes","--log-file","/tmp/log1","/tmp/mix")
print("log1 stdout:", raw(strip(r.stdout)))
print("log1 file:", open("/tmp/log1").read()[:2000] if os.path.exists("/tmp/log1") else "no file")
r=run("aggregate","--stats","--log-file","/tmp/log2","/tmp/mix")  # wrong: log-file is global, must be before aggregate? Actually --log-file after aggregate should error? Let's see
print("log2 test:", raw(r.stdout[:500]), repr(r.stderr[:500]), r.returncode)
# Correct order for aggregate with log-file
r=run("--log-file","/tmp/log2","aggregate","--stats","/tmp/mix")
print("log2 correct:", raw(strip(r.stdout)), repr(r.stderr[:500]), r.returncode)
print(open("/tmp/log2").read()[:3000] if os.path.exists("/tmp/log2") else "no file")
PY"}

# dua (Disk Usage Analyzer)

**dua** is a tool to conveniently learn about the usage of disk space of a given directory. It's parallel by default and will max out your SSD, providing relevant information as fast as possible. Optionally delete superfluous data, and do so more quickly than `rm`.

[![asciicast](https://asciinema.org/a/kDnXUOeqBxZVMoWuFNqzfpeey.svg)](https://asciinema.org/a/kDnXUOeqBxZVMoWuFNqzfpeey)

## Installation

### Binary Release 

#### MacOS

```sh
curl -LSfs https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Byron/dua-cli/master/ci/install.sh | \
    sh -s -- --git Byron/dua-cli --crate dua --tag v2.29.0
```

#### MacOS via [MacPorts](https://www.macports.org):
```sh
sudo port selfupdate

fn clean_path(p: &str) -> String {
    // lexical clean for absolute paths: remove duplicate slashes, '.' and '..', trailing slash (except root)
    // For relative paths, also clean? But ignore-dirs are absolute per help, though relative allowed (no effect). We'll clean generally.
    // If path is empty, return empty.
    if p.is_empty() { return p.to_string(); }
    let is_abs = p.starts_with('/');
    let mut parts: Vec<&str> = Vec::new();
    for comp in p.split('/') {
        if comp.is_empty() || comp == "." {
            continue;
        } else if comp == ".." {
            if !parts.is_empty() && parts.last().unwrap() != &"..") {
                parts.pop();
            } else if !is_abs {
                parts.push("..");
            }
            // for absolute, ignore .. beyond root
        } else {
            parts.push(comp);
        }
    }
    let mut res = String::new();
    if is_abs { res.push('/'); }
    res.push_str(&parts.join("/"));
    if res.is_empty() {
        if is_abs { "/".to_string() } else { ".".to_string() }
    } else {
        res
    }
}

fn canonicalize_or_clean(p: &str) -> String {
    // Try fs::canonicalize, which resolves symlinks and requires existence.
    // If succeeds, return canonical path string. Else, return clean_path.
    // Note: canonicalize returns absolute path with no trailing slash (except root).
    match std::fs::canonicalize(p) {
        Ok(pb) => pb.to_string_lossy().to_string(),
        Err(_) => clean_path(p),
    }
}

        let entry = match entry {
            Ok(e) => e,
            Err(_) => continue,
        };
        let child_path = entry.path();
        let child_str = child_path.to_string_lossy().to_string();
        let basename = entry.file_name().to_string_lossy().to_string();
        // prune symlinks
        let cmeta = match std::fs::symlink_metadata(&child_path) {
            Ok(m) => m,
            Err(_) => continue,
        };
        if cmeta.file_type().is_symlink() {
            continue;
        }
        if cmeta.is_dir() {
            let sz = traverse_path(&child_str, ctx, None, true);
            res.push((basename, sz, true));
        } else {
            let sz = traverse_path(&child_str, ctx, None, false);
            res.push((basename, sz, false));
        }
    }
    Ok(res)
}
